Raindrop Mandalas Tassels & Tibias S’midgins ABOUT SAMHAIN (Pronounced saw-win) Samhain is an ancient Gaelic seasonal festival, and now often celebrated by Wiccan and Pagan cultures. Modern Wicca adopted and reshaped Samhain as one of the eight Sabbats in the Wheel of the Year. Samhain is now considered a major Wiccan Sabbat celebrated from sunset on October 31 to sunset on November 1 to mark the final harvest and the beginning of the Witches' New Year. We celebrate it from October 20th through November 1st at Rae Loft.It is marked the transition from the light half of the year into the dark half. Traditionally, it was associated with the end of the harvest, the beginning of winter, and a liminal time when the boundary between the living and the dead was believed to be especially permeable.One of the best-known Samhain traditions involves large communal fires.Historical accounts describe fires being lit at important gathering places, with people and livestock participating in rituals associated with protection and purification. In later folk traditions, household fires could be extinguished and then rekindled from a communal Samhain fire.Fire symbolized protection, purification, warmth, and the continuation of life through winter.This is where modern Samhain gets much of its association with spirits and ancestors. It is called The Parting of The Veil.In traditional Gaelic belief, Samhain was considered a liminal period. Supernatural beings and the dead were thought to have greater access to the human world. People might leave food or drink for visiting spirits and ancestors. Modern Wiccans and Pagans often reinterpret this as an opportunity to: \Honor deceased loved ones \Remember ancestors \Create an ancestor altar \Light candles for those who have died and to warm the hearth and home in the coming change of season \Reflect on mortality and the cycles of life \Put up and celebrate the harvest Rae Loft is located at 2222 NE Oregon Street, Suite 207 Portland, OR 97232. events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.

events.summary: Fat Over Lean is a free art exhibition celebrating fat bodies, fat artists, and the many ways fatness intersects with queerness, disability, identity, and belonging. Curated by Portland artist Michelle Jackson, the exhibition brings together artwork by over 30 fat artists from across the Pacific Northwest, including painting, photography, fiber, ceramics, mixed media, and more. Created in response to the lack of positive and nuanced representation of fat bodies in the arts, Fat Over Lean is about making space for people whose bodies and experiences are too often left out of galleries. The exhibition will also feature free community events and creative programming throughout October. See works by Alexis Barnes, Ana Mai Luckett, Aurora Owen, Cherie Savoie Tintary, Eko Salamanca, Fi Bu, Garrett Stache, Heather Lobitz, Heather Weitman, Jessie Wu, Jo MahnkeVanHuss, Johnny Sheckler, JUUPI, KT Kusmaul / Body Home Fat Dance, Laura Grae Miller, Lyzz Stewart, M. V. Moran, Madison Flickinger, McKinley Johnson, Michelle Jackson, Morgan Wilhelm, Nat & Jess Breece, Richelle Fullerton, Roselynn La Jeunesse, Ruby Webb, Shaun Crabb, Shayla Smith, Shelby Fercik, Miss Joomina, Sossity Chiricuzio, Stevie Rosman-Hyde, Tarina Bagua, and Uwin Hakan. Join us for these upcoming events: Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3rd, 3- 8 p.m. Why Don't I Draw Myself Fat? Saturday, October 24th from 6 - 7:30 pm. A miniature Art Show and Telltale night of storytelling and taking up space in community hosted by Telltale Presents Closing Reception/Halloween Party: Saturday, October 31st, 7 - 9 pm. About Fat Over Lean Fat Over Lean is a project that aims to lower barriers to the arts for fat, queer, and disabled people by creating opportunities to share their work within the greater Portland, Oregon, and southern Washington communities. Artists were not charged a fee to apply for this show, and they will not pay a commission on artwork sold during the exhibition, aside from standard transaction fees. We believe artists should be able to share their work without having to navigate unnecessary financial barriers. By supporting fat artists, creators, and educators, Fat Over Lean hopes to create more opportunities for growth, visibility, advancement, and connection. This project is about making room: for fat bodies, for queer and disabled voices, for artists who are often asked to take up less space, and for the communities that grow when we get to show up as ourselves. This project was made possible by RACC, Portland Arts & Culture, Fans Only Studio, and Portland Clean Air Committee. Visit Fat Over Lean or Michelle's Instagram for events and gallery hours.

events.summary: Get ready for eight days of frightfully fun festivities as Hallo-Week returns to Vancouver Mall, bringing a full lineup of free, family-friendly Halloween celebrations! events.summary: Your monthly ritual... An invitation to come back to center. Our nervous systems are constantly taking in information. Between work, screens, notifications, responsibilities, and the general pace of everyday life, our attention is often being pulled in multiple directions at once—with very little intentional time to slow down and rest. This monthly nervous system reset is a dedicated space to do exactly that: support nervous system regulation. This immersive sound bath experience uses crystal singing bowls, chimes, oceanic textures, and other therapeutic sounds to gently guide your system out of the noise and stimulation of everyday life and into a deeper state of rest. For 75-minutes, there’s nowhere else you need to be and nothing you need to do. Simply get comfortable, receive the sound, and allow yourself to unwind. Think of this as your recurring monthly ritual to come back to center - a space to intentionally step away from the busyness of life, reconnect with yourself, and give your body and mind the restoration you're craving. Come as you are. Yoga mats, blankets, and props are available for your use, but please feel free to bring anything that will help you feel even more cozy & comfortable. These sessions are open to all; no prior experience is needed. About Kristi Kristi Littman is a certified sound healing practitioner & facilitation teacher whose heart-led approach blends nervous system awareness, intuition, and deep presence. Since 2019, Kristi has held space for thousands of people through community sound baths, corporate wellness, sound healing training, and 1:1 mentorship. She blends crystal singing bowls, chimes, and oceanic tones to create immersive soundscapes designed to soothe the nervous system and realign the body’s natural rhythms. She often weaves in meditation and breathwork, offering grounded, intuitive guidance that helps participants soften, release, and remember their own inner wisdom. Benefits of Sound Therapy: Deep relaxation & stress relief Release tension Energy cleansing & balancing Improved mental focus Enhanced meditation & mindfulness Emotional release Physical healing support Spiritual connection Improved sleep Enhanced creativity & problem-solving Moments of clarity Deep rest
events.title: RITUAL: Immersive Soundbath [Monthly Nervous System Reset] w/Kristi Littman

events.summary: You're Doing it Wrong! is Feeble Flame's handmade, all-ages puppet comedy about trying, failing, and finding your own way. Bitty is a bird with an egg, nowhere to put it, and no idea how every other bird makes nest-building look so easy. Follow Bitty through disastrous neighbor interactions, digging lessons with a prairie dog, and a run-in with a snake. With help from the audience, creative problem-solving, and determination, she finds the home she has been seeking. Expect slapstick, silly sound effects, and a set that has a life of its own. Funded in part by the Jim Henson Foundation, the Regional Arts & Culture Council and the Office of Arts & Culture. Venue: The Studio at Portland Playhouse, 602 NE Prescott St, Portland, OR 97211 Performances: Friday, Oct 23: 11am and 2pm Saturday, Oct 24: 10am and 4pm Sunday, Oct 25: 11am and 2pm Run time: 40 minutes Ages: Geared toward ages 4 and up; fun for everyone! Tickets: Pay what you can: $5, $10, $15, or $20 Audience care: You can leave and come back at any time. A visual guide to the show is published in advance. Feeble Flame is a Portland theater company founded by Ora Fruchter and Sarah Smith, whose work engages audiences of all ages, celebrating curiosity, humor, and imagination. The company's shows are bighearted, funny, and intentionally imperfect, sending the message that there is no one right way to be. This is handmade and delightfully unruly theater for everyone who has ever felt like the instructions were written for somebody else.

events.summary: Will these stories stay behind glass, or will you open a door to the past? Something isn't right here. That book is out of place. There is a card in the display case, but no item behind it. There are antiques in the incorrect place; and artefacts that are standing wrong side up. Clearly, the venue needs your help. As curators of other nearby museums, you are called to the venue after hours in order to help figure out what is causing these disturbances. Once inside, you are greeted by one of the exhibits who has come to life. They are happy to show you around and share tales about the other exhibits. As you hear stories from their lives, it becomes clear that one of them is the culprit behind these disturbances. The question is, which one? Succeed and you will find yourself promoted. Fail, and you may find yourself trapped behind glass forever. Enter an immersive historic experience where exhibits come to life, and there’s a mystery for you to solve! Presented by Live History, a Governor General’s Award nominated international touring theatre company who produces site specific customizable mysteries around the world, and the Oswego Heritage Council.

events.summary: Q&A with Megan Rapinoe to follow screening. Opening night— Toronto International Film Festival 2026 “Revealing… Huntt’s compassionate yet piercing eye gives us a fuller look at who she is than ever before.” — THEWRAP Megan Rapinoe has never separated who she is from what she stands for. A two-time World Cup champion, Olympic gold medalist, proud queer icon and former University of Portland Pilot, she transformed women’s soccer while becoming one of the most fearless voices of her generation. In this intimate, refreshingly unconventional portrait, BEBA director Rebeca Huntt meets Rapinoe at the end of her playing career, looking beyond the public figure to the family, relationships, convictions, victories and failures that shaped her. From coming out and finding freedom in living openly to fighting for equal pay and racial justice, Rapinoe’s story is one of refusing to make herself smaller. Funny, candid and unexpectedly vulnerable, RAPINOE asks what remains when a champion stops competing and begins reckoning with herself. events.summary: Glen Canyon Institute, in collaboration with the Deschutes River Alliance and WaterWatch of Oregon, presents What the River Knows, a Glen Canyon documentary by Good Intentions Paving Co. Today, a lost Eden emerges from beneath Lake Powell, revealing both the consequences of past mistakes and the potential for a new path forward for the Colorado River. What The River Knows explores this pivotal moment, where the urgent need to rethink water management in the West aligns with an opportunity to restore a stunning landscape and flooded ancestral homeland. Amidst the grim discussions surrounding climate change and the Colorado River crisis, the film tells a powerful story of nature’s resilience: Glen Canyon is coming back to life. The evening will open with a documentary short from the Deschutes River Alliance. The Last 100 Miles: The Fight for the lower Deschutes River portrays the degradation of one of the finest trout and salmon sanctuaries anywhere in the world, and the work by those who love the river to save it. Following the film screening, the event will conclude with a panel discussion and audience Q+A.
events.title: What the River Knows, a Colorado River Documentary

events.summary: In the rubble of the London Blitz during World War II, Alice Spencer’s young life is turned upside down as she and her dear friend Alfred are forced to take shelter in an underground tube station. When the ailing Alfred is quarantined, Alice encourages him to escape with her into a book they have cherished since childhood and journey down the rabbit hole to Wonderland. As they travel through the tale, Alice by Heart explores the poignancy of first love, coming to terms with loss, and finding the courage to move forward. A musical about the transformational power of the imagination from the creators of Spring Awakening and Waitress. Ticket Prices: $9 general admission, free for Pacific students. events.summary: Rock, Revolution. *LIZZIE* Brings America's Favorite Murder Mystery to Portland Marin Summer Theater and Bridgetown Conservatory of Musical Theatre present *LIZZIE* Music by Steven Cheslik-deMeyer, Alan Stevens Hewitt & Tim Maner Book and Lyrics by Tim Maner & Steven Cheslik-deMeyer What really happened inside the Borden house? Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. More information and tickets can be found at https:\\\\lizziepdx.com.

events.summary: Step into a slippery world where the line between truth and fiction is all in the packaging. It’s 1936, and a pair of passionate filmmakers have landed their next big project: a sweeping Spanish Civil War film with the potential to change American hearts and minds. It just happens to be bankrolled by the KGB. Spain by Jen Silverman is a seductive and tense thriller about the power of art to change the world – for better and for worse. One of the most ambitious productions in recent Profile history, Spain is a grand cross-disciplinary spectacle featuring multiple partnerships with arts organizations throughout Portland, including live opera developed in partnership with Portland Opera, and both recorded and live music performed by musicians with 45th Parallel!

Theatre opens one hour before showtime. All seats $38. This show is for mature audiences. Nick Lucifer in Club Hell, performed by Sean Lujan (Design for Living, Salomé) and Blavatsky, performed by Anne Sorce (Nice People, Happyness). NICK LUCIFER IN CLUB HELL The story of the universe told by a weathered gangster in “Club Hell” located well down below. BLAVATSKY Madame Blavatsky welcomes you to her private inner quarters to witness truth, lies, psychic phenomena, chickens, monkeys, nonsense, foolishness and drivel. “I’ve always wondered how many great artists have never been recognized. I would venture many. “I believe Don Nigro was a genius of theatre you never heard of” says director Jerry Mouawad. After I selected four of his works earlier this year, Nigro died. The Flying Solo Festival, which features four of his solos, has now become a homage to Nigro’s prolific work - he wrote over 500 plays!” American Theatre’s Lawrence Harbison wrote “he was hardly on the radar. Why not? Don lived in a small house in Northeast Ohio with his father, a disabled veteran who had been seriously wounded in the Battle of the Bulge and needed constant care. So, Don couldn’t travel, making it hard for him to do the sort of networking so important for establishing a reputation. And, anyway, he would rather stay home and write.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences
events.title: October Flight

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.
events.title: Anthropology

Joe Kye will present the world premiere of “through-lineage”, his musical journey into his grandfather’s history in North Korea and beyond.Presented in Reed College’s excellent Greenwood Theater, these fully-realized pieces will push the boundaries of performance as they blend dance, music, film, theater, and storytelling. events.summary: Step into an evening of sacred song with Jai Uttal & Friends, Grammy-nominated world music visionary and beloved pioneer of devotional chanting in the West. With his heart-opening voice, soulful harmonium, and decades of immersion in the path of Bhakti, Jai invites you into a space where music becomes prayer and chanting becomes a bridge to the Divine. Surrounded by fellow musicians and friends, he brings to life a joyful and soulful concert woven with heart-opening kirtan, inspiring stories, and sacred rhythms. Whether you are new to kirtan or a longtime practitioner, you’ll feel at home in this circle of sound. Jai’s music carries the flavors of India, the soul of Brazil, the roots of American folk, and the raw honesty of the devotional heart — weaving a tapestry of sound that is both intimate and expansive. Come ready to raise your voice, to listen deeply, to be carried by rhythm and prayer, and to discover the profound joy of chanting the Divine Names. Kirtan Love Experience with Jai Uttal & Friends — a one-of-a-kind evening of devotion, music, and love.
events.title: Jai Uttal & Open Heart Kirtan with Kavita Kat Macmillan

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. Show Dates: October 15 – November 1, 2026 Thu – Sat at 7:30pm, Sun at 2pm Special Dates: Thursday, October 15 is a preview performance, with discounted tickets. Friday, October 16, is Opening Night! Sat, Oct. 24th – ASL Interpreted Performance Sun, Oct. 25th – Audio Described Performance
events.title: The Woman In Black

events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Night Flight’s Fright Night – A Halloween Circus returns to the historic Alberta Rose Theatre with a queer-gothic-circus spoof of the Phantom of the Opera! Join us for a night of high-flying camp, outrageous scandal, and breathtaking aerial acrobatics. Forget everything you thought you knew about the brooding genius in the mask. Our Phantom isn’t just hiding in the shadows—he’s swinging from the rafters, singing dramatically from the balcony, and desperately trying to seduce the lead baritone while sabotaging every heteronormative trope in sight. Featuring an extraordinary cast of world-class circus artists, this show serves up a wicked cocktail of high-flying danger, sultry gothic horror, and laugh-out-loud comedy. Expect spine-chilling ghostly acrobats on the trapeze, scandalous duets on aerial chains, and contortionists so flexible they make the Phantom’s mood swings look rigid. Will the Phantom win the heart of his muse? Will the diva get her wig on in time? Will the chandelier flatten the front row? Grab your tightest corset, slip into your most dramatic cape, and join us for the ultimate Halloween night out. Whether you’re a lifelong theater geek, a circus fanatic, or just a creature of the night looking for a wildly funny, jaw-dropping show, this year’s Fright Night promises a hauntingly glamorous evening you’ll never forget! Featuring Jack StockLynn of Sir Cupcake’s Queer Circus, Night Flight’s 2026 Fright Night is a Halloween tradition not to be missed! Tickets vanish faster than the Phantom in a puff of stage fog—secure yours before the opera house burns down!

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: Portland favorites Tree Frogs bring their eclectic blend of roots rock, improvisation, and groove-driven songwriting to Tomorrow's Verse for an evening of music shaped by decades of playing together. Drawing from rock, country, folk, blues, funk, and soul, the band has built a reputation for shows that feel both relaxed and adventurous, where strong songs provide the foundation for unexpected musical turns. A fixture of the Pacific Northwest music scene since the early 1990s, Tree Frogs spent much of that decade on the road, playing more than 500 shows across the U.S. and Europe in support of three releases: Tree Frogs Live! (1994), Leap Year (1996), and Live at the Laurelthirst (1997). After taking a break from touring, the band returned in 2000 and has remained a steady presence at clubs, festivals, and neighborhood venues throughout the region ever since. What sets Tree Frogs apart isn't virtuosity or spectacle, but chemistry. Years of shared stages have given the band a natural musical connection that allows songs to stretch, breathe, and evolve in the moment. One tune might lean into a deep country groove, while the next finds its way toward funk, blues, or classic rock territory. Whether you're a longtime fan or catching them for the first time, expect an evening of road-tested musicianship, thoughtful songwriting, and the kind of warm, communal atmosphere that has kept Northwest audiences coming back for years.
events.title: Tree Frogs

events.summary: Will these stories stay behind glass, or will you open a door to the past? Something isn't right here. That book is out of place. There is a card in the display case, but no item behind it. There are antiques in the incorrect place; and artefacts that are standing wrong side up. Clearly, the venue needs your help. As curators of other nearby museums, you are called to the venue after hours in order to help figure out what is causing these disturbances. Once inside, you are greeted by one of the exhibits who has come to life. They are happy to show you around and share tales about the other exhibits. As you hear stories from their lives, it becomes clear that one of them is the culprit behind these disturbances. The question is, which one? Succeed and you will find yourself promoted. Fail, and you may find yourself trapped behind glass forever. Enter an immersive historic experience where exhibits come to life, and there’s a mystery for you to solve! Presented by Live History, a Governor General’s Award nominated international touring theatre company who produces site specific customizable mysteries around the world, and the Oswego Heritage Council.
events.title: Behind Glass Escape Room

events.summary: 34 Years Later: A Seattle Pearl Jam Celebration Washed in Black is stoked to be back at Billy Blues Bar & Grill for a very special night celebrating Pearl Jam, Seattle music history, and the community that has kept this music alive for more than three decades. October 1990 marked the very beginning of Pearl Jam as a live band in Seattle — from their first show at the Off Ramp to the early rehearsal and demo sessions that helped launch one of the most important bands of the era. 34 years later, we’re celebrating those Seattle roots — just south in Vancouver. Washed in Black will take the stage for an epic live Pearl Jam experience, digging beyond the hits and deep into the catalog with rarities, deep cuts, fan favorites, and songs you don’t hear every night. If you miss the days when flannel was king and the Seattle sound was changing rock music forever, this one is for you. SPECIAL GUEST: NICK MARDON TRIO We’re fired up to have our very own Nick Mardon bringing the Nick Mardon Trio out to kick off the night. The Seattle-based blues-rock power trio features Nick Mardon on guitar and vocals, Adin Pennington on bass and vocals, and Andy Emery on drums. Their sound blends the raw power of ’60s and ’70s blues-rock with the Seattle sound of the 1990s. After hundreds of shows throughout the Pacific Northwest, they’ve built a massive repertoire featuring original music along with timeless covers from artists including Jimi Hendrix, Stevie Ray Vaughan, Led Zeppelin, Pearl Jam, Sublime, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Eric Clapton, Johnny Cash and more. Come early. Catch Nick Mardon Trio. Stay for the definitive Pearl Jam tribute experience. SATURDAY, OCTOBER 24 Billy Blues Bar & Grill 7115 NE Hazel Dell Ave Vancouver, WA Doors: 7 PM Show: 8 PM $15 at the door 21\+ WASHED IN BLACK — A TRIBUTE TO PEARL JAM NICK MARDON TRIO — Originals & Timeless Covers BACK IN THE PORTLAND / VANCOUVER SCENE. Relive some memories. Make some new ones. Make America Grunge Again. Salud!

events.summary: Daði Freyr is an Icelandic singer, songwriter, and producer known for his witty lyricism, infectious synth-pop, and joyful unpredictability. He rose to global attention with his 2020 hit "Think About Things", which went viral during lockdown, earning over 100 million streams and praise from P!nk, James Corden, and Russell Crowe. His new album Too Much, Not Enough, out May 8th, marks a new chapter. Co-written with collaborators for the first time, it's his most emotionally honest work yet: a record about self-acceptance, about being who you actually are rather than who you think others want to see. After years in Berlin, Daði returned to Iceland in 2025, and that sense of coming home, of settling into something real, runs through every track. This autumn, Daði brings his live show to the US and Canada. Performing alone on stage with self-built instruments and hand-crafted visuals, it's an intimate, one-of-a-kind experience and the connection with his audience remains, as ever, the thing he loves most.

events.summary: From behind the redwood curtain of Humboldt County, California, the seven piece funk-soul band Diggin Dirt has carved out a niche as a live party not to be missed. Shoveling their own path, Diggin Dirt has seen sustained growth over the past few years, with multiple national tours and festival stops at Jam Cruise, High Sierra, Hulaween, Same Same but Different, Live Oak, Cascade Equinox, Joshua Tree Music Festival and many more. Per a 2024 Jam Cruise writer, “This was the soul music I grew up with in the ‘60s and ‘70s, but I confess I wasn’t expecting \[Diggin Dirt\] to be throwing it down this hard. This group is impossibly tight, and Zach Alder might be the best soul shouter I’ve ever heard, and I’ve heard a few.” Their infectious sound is fueled by blazing horns, searing guitars and a relentlessly driving rhythm section, and tying it all together is the band’s frontman who launches the ensemble into rarefied air with his pipes, charisma and natural-born soul. With flashes of James Brown or Sly and the Family Stone, Otis Redding or Tower of Power, the band’s sound is both familiar and yet refreshingly original, layering psychedelic rock, Motown soul, afrobeat and even reggae atop a thick foundation of late-60s inspired funk.

events.summary: Director and QDoc alum, Jeffrey Schwarz in attendance. WORLD PREMIERE — TRIBECA FESTIVAL 2026 “Captures a poignant tipping point in pre-AIDS queer culture.” — Guy Lodge, Variety In 1979, William Friedkin descended on New York’s West Village to make Cruising, his controversial thriller starring Al Pacino as a cop hunting a serial killer in the city’s gay leather bars. The production ignited fierce protests from queer activists who feared the film would turn gay men into predators and victims at a moment when the community was fighting for visibility and dignity. But behind the Hollywood controversy was a real-life tragedy. Jeffrey Schwarz (VITO, TAB HUNTER CONFIDENTIAL) traces the story of Addison Verrill, a young Variety reporter murdered in 1977 after a night at the Mineshaft, while revisiting the vanished world of pre-AIDS New York that surrounded him. Part true crime, part queer cultural history, Mineshaft asks what gets remembered when Hollywood turns real lives into fiction. KINDLY SPONSORED BY HOWIE BIERBAUM, TOM BARRETO & BRIAN SINCLAIR.
events.title: MINESHAFT: THE CRUISING MURDERS

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: Get moving with a beginner Tai Chi class by Many Roads Martial Arts Center on Sundays. 10:30 – 11:30 AM | Sundays, May 3 – October 25, 2026 Many Roads Martial Arts Center is offering an introductory Tai Chi class at Lan Su on Sundays at 10:30AM. This class will introduce the fundamental principles of Tai Chi Chaun \(or Taijiquan\) using the Yang Style 24 Posture Form. We will work on posture and body alignment alongside principles of movement and meditation. We will also discuss how Tai Chi blends health, meditation, and martial application. This class is suitable for all levels but will be particularly helpful for beginners of all ages. Get Admission Meet the Instructors: Many Roads Martial Arts Center Jenny Lohr, Owner/Instructor Jenny has been practicing Shaolin Kung Fu and Tai Chi since 2005. As the owner of Many Roads Martial Arts Center, her focus is nurturing a supportive and safe learning environment while challenging everyone to keep growing and improving. Jenny loves the physical and mental challenges of martial arts and is very excited to share them with the students and instructors at the center. Jay Twitchell, Instructor Jay has studied various martial arts systems including boxing, wrestling, judo, karate, taekwondo, aikido, hopkido, kumdo, and muay thai kick boxing since he was 10. In other words, he has been used as a punching bag for over 30 years by masters and lifelong practitioners of these systems. His lifetime of experience getting kicked, punched, choked, kneed, elbowed, and thrown are invaluable in teaching others how not to be. Balancing his martial studies, Jay has 20 years of experience as a massage therapist and movement specialist, offering him a deep knowledge of the human body and healthy practice. Myk Olsen, Instructor Myk has been a Tai Chi Chuan practitioner since 1997 and has been teaching since 2013. His primary teachers were Gao Jamin and Yu Shaowen. Over the years, Myk has learned a multitude of forms in Yang, Chen, Wu, and Sun styles—both open-hand and weapons \(straight sword, broadsword, staff, spear, cane, deerhorn knives, and daggers\). While he used to compete in both forms and Push-Hands, Myk now focuses more time on teaching. His teaching style is student-centered and is focused on achieving a balance between the meditative and martial aspects of the forms. Myk also teaches a Tai Chi class specifically geared toward those with mobility and balance issues on Sunday afternoon. Joel, Instructor A lifetime student of martial arts, Joel has been training Shaolin Kung Fu and Tai Chi since 1999 and teaching since 2009. His teaching goal is to provide tools to improve every student’s physical, mental, and emotional health in a supportive, encouraging learning environment. Joel’s primary teaching focus is Chen Tai Chi as taught by Master George Xu \(Xu Guo Ming\). He also teaches our black belt Shaolin curriculum, Yang style Tai Chi, and 5 Element Qi Gong. events.summary: You're Doing it Wrong! is Feeble Flame's handmade, all-ages puppet comedy about trying, failing, and finding your own way. Follow Bitty through disastrous neighbor interactions, digging lessons with a prairie dog, and a run-in with a snake. With help from the audience, creative problem-solving, and determination, she finds the home she has been seeking. Expect slapstick, silly sound effects, and a set that has a life of its own. Funded in part by the Jim Henson Foundation, the Regional Arts & Culture Council and the Office of Arts & Culture. Venue: The Studio at Portland Playhouse, 602 NE Prescott St, Portland, OR 97211 Performances: Friday, Oct 23: 11am and 2pm Saturday, Oct 24: 10am and 4pm Sunday, Oct 25: 11am and 2pm Run time: 40 minutes Ages: Geared toward ages 4 and up; fun for everyone! Tickets: Pay what you can: $5, $10, $15, or $20 Audience care: You can leave and come back at any time. A visual guide to the show is published in advance. Feeble Flame is a Portland theater company founded by Ora Fruchter and Sarah Smith, whose work engages audiences of all ages, celebrating curiosity, humor, and imagination. The company's shows are bighearted, funny, and intentionally imperfect, sending the message that there is no one right way to be. This is handmade and delightfully unruly theater for everyone who has ever felt like the instructions were written for somebody else.

events.summary: Q&A with QDoc alums Director Jennifer Kroot and Editor Bill Weber, joined by Sister Roma, Sister Lida, and Honey Mahogany to follow the screening. “In a time of uncertainty and anguish, HUNKY JESUS is balm for the soul.” — Gavin Spoors, FILMHOUNDS Every Easter Sunday in San Francisco, the Sisters of Perpetual Indulgence turn celebration into an act of resistance. Director, Jennifer M. Kroot (THE UNTOLD TALES OF ARMISTEAD MAUPIN, TO BE TAKEI) dives into the annual tradition where drag, burlesque, religious parody and outrageous pageantry collide in an expression of queer community and radical joy. Anchored in the 2023 celebration, the film blends performances, candid interviews and rare archival footage to trace four decades of the Sisters’ fearless activism, from confronting the Catholic Church to advocating for those pushed to the margins. With Sister Roma, RUPAUL’S DRAG RACE alum Honey Mahogany, and voiceover by George Takei, HUNKY JESUS is funny, irreverent and unexpectedly moving, celebrating a community that has made an art form of challenging hypocrisy while welcoming everyone to the party. Raindrop Mandalas Tassels & Tibias S’midgins ABOUT SAMHAIN (Pronounced saw-win) Samhain is an ancient Gaelic seasonal festival, and now often celebrated by Wiccan and Pagan cultures. Modern Wicca adopted and reshaped Samhain as one of the eight Sabbats in the Wheel of the Year. Samhain is now considered a major Wiccan Sabbat celebrated from sunset on October 31 to sunset on November 1 to mark the final harvest and the beginning of the Witches' New Year. We celebrate it from October 20th through November 1st at Rae Loft.It is marked the transition from the light half of the year into the dark half. Traditionally, it was associated with the end of the harvest, the beginning of winter, and a liminal time when the boundary between the living and the dead was believed to be especially permeable.One of the best-known Samhain traditions involves large communal fires.Historical accounts describe fires being lit at important gathering places, with people and livestock participating in rituals associated with protection and purification. In later folk traditions, household fires could be extinguished and then rekindled from a communal Samhain fire.Fire symbolized protection, purification, warmth, and the continuation of life through winter.This is where modern Samhain gets much of its association with spirits and ancestors. It is called The Parting of The Veil.In traditional Gaelic belief, Samhain was considered a liminal period. Supernatural beings and the dead were thought to have greater access to the human world. People might leave food or drink for visiting spirits and ancestors. Modern Wiccans and Pagans often reinterpret this as an opportunity to: \Honor deceased loved ones \Remember ancestors \Create an ancestor altar \Light candles for those who have died and to warm the hearth and home in the coming change of season \Reflect on mortality and the cycles of life \Put up and celebrate the harvest Rae Loft is located at 2222 NE Oregon Street, Suite 207 Portland, OR 97232. No outside beverages permitted. All ages. Sorry, no dogs - we have one that works here who is healing from cancer surgery.

events.summary: Fat Over Lean is a free art exhibition celebrating fat bodies, fat artists, and the many ways fatness intersects with queerness, disability, identity, and belonging. Curated by Portland artist Michelle Jackson, the exhibition brings together artwork by over 30 fat artists from across the Pacific Northwest, including painting, photography, fiber, ceramics, mixed media, and more. Created in response to the lack of positive and nuanced representation of fat bodies in the arts, Fat Over Lean is about making space for people whose bodies and experiences are too often left out of galleries. The exhibition will also feature free community events and creative programming throughout October. See works by Alexis Barnes, Ana Mai Luckett, Aurora Owen, Cherie Savoie Tintary, Eko Salamanca, Fi Bu, Garrett Stache, Heather Lobitz, Heather Weitman, Jessie Wu, Jo MahnkeVanHuss, Johnny Sheckler, JUUPI, KT Kusmaul / Body Home Fat Dance, Laura Grae Miller, Lyzz Stewart, M. V. Moran, Madison Flickinger, McKinley Johnson, Michelle Jackson, Morgan Wilhelm, Nat & Jess Breece, Richelle Fullerton, Roselynn La Jeunesse, Ruby Webb, Shaun Crabb, Shayla Smith, Shelby Fercik, Miss Joomina, Sossity Chiricuzio, Stevie Rosman-Hyde, Tarina Bagua, and Uwin Hakan. Join us for these upcoming events: Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3rd, 3- 8 p.m. Why Don't I Draw Myself Fat? Saturday, October 24th from 6 - 7:30 pm. A miniature Art Show and Telltale night of storytelling and taking up space in community hosted by Telltale Presents Closing Reception/Halloween Party: Saturday, October 31st, 7 - 9 pm. About Fat Over Lean Fat Over Lean is a project that aims to lower barriers to the arts for fat, queer, and disabled people by creating opportunities to share their work within the greater Portland, Oregon, and southern Washington communities. Artists were not charged a fee to apply for this show, and they will not pay a commission on artwork sold during the exhibition, aside from standard transaction fees. We believe artists should be able to share their work without having to navigate unnecessary financial barriers. By supporting fat artists, creators, and educators, Fat Over Lean hopes to create more opportunities for growth, visibility, advancement, and connection. This project is about making room: for fat bodies, for queer and disabled voices, for artists who are often asked to take up less space, and for the communities that grow when we get to show up as ourselves. This project was made possible by RACC, Portland Arts & Culture, Fans Only Studio, and Portland Clean Air Committee. Visit Fat Over Lean or Michelle's Instagram for events and gallery hours.

events.summary: We Built You a Garden is the third installment of Metro’s Community Voices project, a multimedia storytelling initiative that invites residents of Metro Affordable Housing Bond-funded communities to explore the meaning of home through photography, writing and collective reflection. Hosted through a summer workshop series at the Strong Empowerment Village in partnership with artists Gwen Hoeffgen and Domenic Toliver, the project centers the experiences of residents with ties to North and Northeast Portland. Through weekly workshops and the use of film photography and creative writing, participants documented places, people and memories that shape their understanding of home, legacy and belonging. Their work considers displacement, resilience and community history, creating a powerful collection of stories that honor the past while imagining what can continue to grow. Ultimately, We Built You a Garden asks what’s been inherited, what’s been built, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. It speaks to the ongoing impact of displacement in Portland for the Black community, but it also affirms what it took — and continues to take — to nourish, tend and build home. Exhibition and events: Free admission Oct. 9, 5:30pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Exhibition Opening at The BLACK Gallery Join us for the opening of We Built You a Garden, with remarks and refreshments as well as free copies of the project’s publication. Open to public with remarks from Metro, artists, and Don’t Shoot PDX . Oct. 23, 6pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Community Conversation at The BLACK Gallery A conversation about the past, present, and future of Portland through the experiences of the people who live, work, organize, and build here. Artists, activists, community members, youth and Metro come together to consider what we have inherited, what we have built, what is changing, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. The BLACK Gallery will be open to the public on the following Sundays from 1pm to 4pm during the exhibition’s display: Oct. 11, Oct. 18, Oct. 25 and Nov. 1.
events.title: We Built You a Garden

events.summary: Q SHORTS | SUNDAY, OCT 25, 1:30PM Three fantastic short docs celebrating the unique and bold stories of our diverse community. FILM 1: RAINBOW RIDER Outspoken lesbian trucker Shelle Lichti crisscrosses America behind the wheel of the Rainbow Rider, her unmistakable Pride-wrapped 18-wheeler, with her chihuahua riding shotgun. Facing hostility, middle fingers and the occasional unexpected ally, Shelle turns life on the road into a mission of visibility, connection and community for LGBTQ+ truckers. events.summary: You're Doing it Wrong! is Feeble Flame's handmade, all-ages puppet comedy about trying, failing, and finding your own way. Bitty is a bird with an egg, nowhere to put it, and no idea how every other bird makes nest-building look so easy. Follow Bitty through disastrous neighbor interactions, digging lessons with a prairie dog, and a run-in with a snake. With help from the audience, creative problem-solving, and determination, she finds the home she has been seeking. Expect slapstick, silly sound effects, and a set that has a life of its own. Funded in part by the Jim Henson Foundation, the Regional Arts & Culture Council and the Office of Arts & Culture. Venue: The Studio at Portland Playhouse, 602 NE Prescott St, Portland, OR 97211 Performances: Friday, Oct 23: 11am and 2pm Saturday, Oct 24: 10am and 4pm Sunday, Oct 25: 11am and 2pm Run time: 40 minutes Ages: Geared toward ages 4 and up; fun for everyone! Tickets: Pay what you can: $5, $10, $15, or $20 Audience care: You can leave and come back at any time. A visual guide to the show is published in advance. Feeble Flame is a Portland theater company founded by Ora Fruchter and Sarah Smith, whose work engages audiences of all ages, celebrating curiosity, humor, and imagination. The company's shows are bighearted, funny, and intentionally imperfect, sending the message that there is no one right way to be. This is handmade and delightfully unruly theater for everyone who has ever felt like the instructions were written for somebody else.
events.title: You're Doing it Wrong!

Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. Nick Lucifer in Club Hell, performed by Sean Lujan (Design for Living, Salomé) and Blavatsky, performed by Anne Sorce (Nice People, Happyness). NICK LUCIFER IN CLUB HELL The story of the universe told by a weathered gangster in “Club Hell” located well down below. BLAVATSKY Madame Blavatsky welcomes you to her private inner quarters to witness truth, lies, psychic phenomena, chickens, monkeys, nonsense, foolishness and drivel. “I’ve always wondered how many great artists have never been recognized. I would venture many. “I believe Don Nigro was a genius of theatre you never heard of” says director Jerry Mouawad. After I selected four of his works earlier this year, Nigro died. The Flying Solo Festival, which features four of his solos, has now become a homage to Nigro’s prolific work - he wrote over 500 plays!” American Theatre’s Lawrence Harbison wrote “he was hardly on the radar. Why not? Don lived in a small house in Northeast Ohio with his father, a disabled veteran who had been seriously wounded in the Battle of the Bulge and needed constant care. So, Don couldn’t travel, making it hard for him to do the sort of networking so important for establishing a reputation. And, anyway, he would rather stay home and write.” Production Credits: *Light Design:* Ronnie Rantis Costume Design: Laura Helgeson Sound Design: Myrrh Larsen Note: For Mature Audiences

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. Show Dates: October 15 – November 1, 2026 Thu – Sat at 7:30pm, Sun at 2pm Special Dates: Thursday, October 15 is a preview performance, with discounted tickets. Friday, October 16, is Opening Night! events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: End your weekend slowly with sound, sauna, and rest. Join us at Koti, a neighborhood Finnish sauna tucked into a quiet residential neighborhood in Milwaukie, for a Sunday evening of sound, warmth, and time to unwind. We'll begin with an immersive 60-minute sound bath led by Kristi Littman. Through the resonant sounds of crystal singing bowls, you'll have an opportunity to settle in, quiet your mind, and enjoy an hour of uninterrupted rest. Afterward, we'll head outside for two unhurried hours of traditional Finnish sauna, cold plunging, and time around the fire. In Finland, sauna is an ordinary and cherished part of everyday life. It's a place to slow down, connect with others, and enjoy the simple pleasure of getting warm. At Koti, we've brought that tradition into our own backyard, with a cedar sauna, the gentle steam of löyly, fresh-water cold plunges, and space to enjoy the outdoors. There's no prescribed routine or pace to follow. Enjoy the heat, cool off when you're ready, sit by the fire, and settle into the evening however feels good to you. What to bring: Please bring a yoga mat for the sound bath. You're also welcome to bring a blanket, pillow, warm socks, or anything else that makes you extra comfortable. Bring your swimsuit and two towels (one small one for sitting on in the sauna and one for drying off). All are welcome. No prior sound bath or sauna experience is needed.
events.title: Sunday Slowdown: Sound Bath + Sauna

events.summary: See the award-winning short documentary featuring a beloved Portland icon, then join a post-screening walking tour to view the Thompson Elk and other monuments that shape the story of our city. At the Portland Art Museum. Film begins at 4:00pm. Tour Begins at 5:00pm. Event is part of the ADX Festival. About the Film: The Elk - 30 min Documentary As protest consumed Portland, Ore. in 2020, the city removed a beloved elk sculpture for safekeeping. Six years later, the elk is the first of the city's damaged monuments to return, and the only sculpture without controversy. But in a city that never really stopped protesting, people remain divided over why the elk went away—and what it means for the dinged-up but refurbished symbol to finally return. Set in an American city reckoning with its symbols of westward expansion, the unfolding fate of the elk and the other sculptures tells the story of a nation divided over who and what belongs on a pedestal. About the Walking Tour: Tour guide Sarah Gilbert of Around Portland Tours is a featured participant in the film, The Elk. Sarah is a writer and bicycle evangelist, and has worked in the hiking tourism industry for over a decade. Join Sarah and Director Erika Bolstad on a localized tour of downtown Portland monuments, including the Thompson Elk. The tour is free and starts immediately after the screening and Q&A for The Elk, outside the Portland Art Museum.
events.title: The Elk - Film Screening and Walking Tour

events.summary: Sundays 4:30PM - 5:30PM, Oct 4 - Dec 20 | $10/weekly drop in Need a reset for your busy week ahead? Join us Sunday late afternoons for a welcoming, beginner-friendly yoga class focused on foundational poses, mindful movement, breath awareness, and building confidence on the mat. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this class is designed to help you build a strong foundation through accessible movement, breath work, and foundational poses. We’ll focus on alignment, balance, flexibility, and body awareness in a welcoming, supportive environment. Beginners are encouraged to join, and those with a regular practice will also benefit from slowing down, refining technique, and deepening their understanding of familiar poses. Options and modifications will be offered throughout class so everyone can move at their own pace. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring a yoga mat if possible \(a limited number will be available to borrow\), and please arrive 5–10 minutes before class begins so we can start on time. Classes are led by Wyle O'Neill, from Love Our Practice, whose yoga journey began in high school and later led him to study in Mysore and Goa, India, where he deepened his understanding of yoga’s roots and philosophy. Wyle completed his 200-hour RYT training at Yoga Salt with Tamal Dodge and completed his 500-hour teacher training at Sthira Yoga School in Goa, India. His teaching blends accessible movement, meditation, breathwork through an individual-centered practice to help students feel grounded, present, as well as connected to themselves and community.

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026

events.summary: Dava and Barr Pennington, professors at a Midwestern university, both harbor potent secrets. Fiction writing is his specialty, English literature is hers. But Dava is unhappy in their marriage, and secretly in love with a colleague, Svetlana White, who teaches in the Russian Studies department; spurred by their complicated liaison, she spends her nights working on a novel about two women who run a domestic violence shelter in coastal Maine. Though she loves the work and the refuge it provides, the writing becomes increasingly difficult as her memory begins to fail; tests reveal that she’s suffering from early-onset Alzheimer’s. After a precipitous decline, she moves to a memory care facility in a neighboring town. Soon afterward, her husband, alone in the house at night, discovers her hidden manuscript, which he reads with envy, and then with anger, as he extrapolates his wife’s affair from the relationship described in the novel’s pages. Over the next two years he rewrites the novel and publishes it as his own, to wide acclaim. But persistent feelings of guilt lead him to confess his theft to an unlikely party, who leads others to the truth. Luna, Phoenix, Queen \(Knopf\) tells its tale of artistic and marital betrayal in a chorus of voices. We hear from Barr as he becomes obsessed with Luna, a horrifically injured dog at a local shelter; from Dava as she meets Svetlana for the first time, on a transatlantic flight to Dublin; from Milo, Dava’s son, as he hides in the woods with Naomi, Svetlana’s daughter; from Svetlana, experiencing the loss of a relationship that ended before it could come to fruition; from Evie, Barr’s research assistant, who witnessed Dava’s last days at home with her husband; from James, the Penningtons’ younger son, who makes a startling discovery after his father’s death; and from Milo and Svetlana again, as they grieve the injustice of Barr’s theft and confront the devastation of Dava’s disease. In a narrative that spans four decades and four thousand miles, Luna, Phoenix, Queen — by Julie Orringer, bestselling author of The Invisible Bridge — illuminates the power of storytelling and explores the terror of losing the ability to make sense of our world. It is a cry of rage against our vulnerability and helplessness; an acknowledgment of the mysteries beneath the familiar surface of our world; and ultimately, if unexpectedly, a radical testament to love in its many forms. Orringer will be joined in conversation by Kimberly King Parsons, author of We Were the Universe. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/julie-orringer-9798217207886
events.title: Powell's Presents: Julie Orringer in Conversation With Kimberly King Parsons

events.summary: Some words from other folks on the new record “below your knows” No dog ever eats Luke Callen’s homework. He does it all. He turns it in ahead of time. Not for a grade. Not for extra credit. It’s his work and he’s good at it. Poet. Singer. Player. Just listen. First he captures your attention. You want to make comparisons with the giants whose shoulders he stood on. But don’t. He’s plenty tall enough in his own bare feet and his shoulders are wide enough to hold up the next batch of poets, singers, players. Keep listening. Now he captures your imagination. Luke is the hitch-hiker who picks you up. Get in. Toss your bindle in the back. Have you got a couple bucks for gas? No matter. He’s going take you all around the world. Pay attention. He’s going to show you everything that’s in it. And it’s right Below Your Knows. -Eddie Allen Below your knows gets better with every listen. The album has a great atmosphere, it is one of those rarities that once you start it, you have to listen to the end. It is a standout, I get the same feeling from this album as I get from listening to albums like Dead Kennedy’s – Bedtime for Democracy, or Grateful Dead – Live/Dead, or Al Scorch – Circle Round the Signs. Below your knows takes you on a sonic journey and hits the listener in their soul. It is amazing, the music connects you with a “life force”…to others, the Earth, and the stars. The songs are something special; they feel so genuine and heartfelt. It’s truly rare to find music like this out there these days. The songs take one on an introspective journey and forces you to answer the question “Are you fucking alive?!”. By the time the album finishes, you are left with the question….what next? Hit Fucking Play. – Eric Peloza Take heed, take heed, Luke Callen has a great new song “a walk out of doors” from his upcoming album, Below Your Knows. An album built out of the roots that once was American folk music. It’s simple, earthy, and raw. “A walk out of doors” is the first track off the album and it is nothing short of a masterpiece. It’s beautiful and gritty. I don’t know if it’s the tonal quality of the resonator, or Callen’s vocals, but I could listen to this song ten thousand times and never grow tired. The lyrics paint a beautiful picture, the resonator places you within the picture, and Callen’s voice makes it so you never want to leave. I feel like I’m sitting down around a campfire listening to Callen as if he’s right there in front of me. It’s incredibly intimate and I want nothing more than to witness him performing the song live. – lttlbrthr Luke Callen is originally from the river town of La Crosse, WI-the heart of the Driftless Region-and currently lives in Minneapolis, MN by way of Colorado. A teller of tall tales and a singer of short tunes-Luke lugs around a couple of guitars-a few harmonicas and even a banjo if he has to. A simple writer and liver who cares more about his cast irons than he does about his interweb streams-Luke is now on tour and will be for the foreseeable future. To track him down and see a live show for yourself…please just get in touch. Having steeped himself-like a cheap bag of tea that you found in a drawer you rarely open-in the recording’s of Harry Smith’s Anthology of American Folk Music, to campfires, classrooms, honky tonks, festivals and clubs across the country, Luke brings his humble sense of humor and humanity. With his Chevy Astro greased up, Luke has played hundreds of shows spanning both coasts, the American west, south and heartland. He has had the opportunity to provide support for Dom Flemons, Dead Horses, The Dustbowl Revival, Kacy & Clayton, James McMurtry, Whiskey Shivers, Charlie Parr, The Lowest Pair, The Last Revel, Lilly Hiatt, Chicago Farmer, and Robbie Fulks among others.
events.title: Luke Callen & Bad Posture Club

events.summary: Join us for a special FREE SHOW with Dusk Dept. and special guest Greaterkind \+ A Very Good DJ Set from Alex Wasily! No names, no faces, just grooves. Dusk Dept. is a seven-piece collective emerging from the deep corners of the modern funk underground…a shadowy convergence of musicians whose fingerprints can be found on the grooves of the heaviest hitters in the lineage of rhythm. Formed unofficially from the raging of late night sessions that transformed into full-fledged studio recordings, Dusk Dept. keeps its members hidden beneath black hoods, trading ego & resumes for atmosphere, and identity for collective creating. Onstage, the robes blur every boundary…between player and audience, between band and ritual, between now and the memory of some older recording that felt cutting edge that you just discovered that you now can’t remember. Their debut, a self-titled album on Ear Up Records (founded by Jeff Coffin of the Dave Matthews Band), sounds like the meeting point of the sacred and the filthy; analog funk baptized in mystery. Seven players. Seven voices. One department in charge of the night shift. Dusk Dept. doesn’t announce itself. It appears… an injection of brass, a thump of bass, a silhouette under dim lights. Then it’s gone, leaving behind only sweat, grooves, and questions.

events.summary:
Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session: drink your beverage of choice, bring your laptop, and hang out with your peers! Have engaging conversations, or focus on work or projects. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work.

---- Schedule ----

You're welcome to drop in anytime during the event. We understand that everyone may have external commitments and challenges - join us when you can!

We have informal unscheduled introductions - practice your personal elevator pitch, or take things slower to build your confidence.

---- Venue ----

Fly Chai allow us to informally and freely use their space. If within your budget, we'd appreciate your help to sustain our use of the venue, by purchasing something tasty, whether Chai or otherwise.

Find us at tables with a Code&Coffee sign - or a clump of laptop-users!

Wifi and power outlets are available.
Our meeting area should be accessible - please let us know if not.

---- What to expect ----

Smaller events than you may be used to, with a mixed crowd week-to-week. We expect this is likely due to us meeting weekly, at a less central location.

These may result in what you're looking for:
    A smaller, less intimidating, lower pressure, cozy atmosphere.
    A mix of regular and new faces.
    A simpler schedule - every week, same time, same place - that you can drop into when you like.
    Being closer to you than other events.

Whether those are generally or partly to your liking, we hope you'll consider dropping by sometime!

---- Getting to the venue ----

Look for the venue on the meetup Google map, or alternatives like OpenStreetMap.

-- Driving --

There are limited parking spaces on a lot outside the venue (4+1 accessible), with more in the surrounding area.

-- Transit options --

Beaverton Central (Red/Blue MAX), then walk~ 8 minutes

Beaverton Transit Center (Red/Blue MAX, bus, WES) then walk ~11 minutes

For a shorter walk to the venue, take a bus from Beaverton Transit Center (52 to Farmington/Hall, 76 to Watson/Broadway, 57 to Canyon/Watson)
events.title: Code & Coffee - Beaverton

events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: From the Booker Prize-winning and bestselling author of Shuggie Bain and Young Mungo comes a vivid, moving novel following a young man returning to his Hebridean island home, a portrait of a father’s expectations and a son’s desires. Out of money and with little to show for his art school education, John-Calum Macleod takes the ferry back home to the Isle of Harris in the Outer Hebrides to find that little has changed except for him. He returns to the windswept croft and the two pillars of his childhood: his father John, a sheep farmer, tweed weaver, and lay preacher in the local Presbyterian church, and his maternal grandmother Ella, a profanity-loving Glaswegian whose steady warmth helped Cal weather the sudden departure of his mother. Cal privately wonders if any lonely men might be found on the barren hillsides of home, while John is dismayed by his son’s long hair, strange clothes, and seeming unwillingness to be Saved. But Cal isn't the only one in the croft house who is keeping secrets. As lambing season turns to shearing season, the threads holding together the community together become increasingly frayed, and nothing will remain as it was before. John of John \(Grove Press\) is a singular novel about duty, passion, and the transformative power of the truth. It is a magnificent literary work that cements Douglas Stuart's reputation as one of our greatest novelists working today. Stuart will be joined in conversation by Omar El Akkad, author of One Day, Everyone Will Have Always Been Against This. Buy the book: https://www.powells.com/events/douglas-stuart-9780802167194
