events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: The Literary Arts Bookstore and Cafe are thrilled to welcome Lit Mic for another immersive writing workshop! Participants will search for clues, interview witnesses, and conduct their own investigation via creative writing prompts and sharing to solve the murder. Detective Jack Argentine is back, and this time, it’s magical. It’s nearly Halloween, and a coven of honest-to-goodness witches is hosting their Biannual Bewitchment Ball. But something has gone terribly wrong, and one of the coven members is dead! Through independent and guided writing prompts, investigation, and conversations with live witchy actors, it’s up to YOU to help Detective Argentine figure out if this is just a spell gone wrong… or a case of Halloween Homicide. But the witching hour is close at hand; if the clock strikes midnight, the witches will be gone back to their home, and this case will vanish like mist in the night. Are you up for the task? About Lit Mic: Portland Lit Mic is a community-oriented organization, dedicated to getting writers from all backgrounds together. Founded as a writers-only open mic by Portland State Alumni Jordan Marzka and Grace Lawrence, the two have gone on to plan and host immersive writing workshops and reading series. You can catch their open mic every second Friday of the month at Rose City Book Pub, or keep up on their current events by following their Instagram @portlandlitmic Content warning—while Murder in the Bookstore is intended to be fun for all, themes of murder/violence and mild gore will be present. events.summary: Although he was born in the industrial heart of New Jersey, Red’s mother Maggie made damn sure that he would be reared on folk and country music. She served up a steady diet of Country tunes from Karen Dalton to Patsy Cline to Dwight Yoakam on the kitchen radio day after day. Red’s father, a lifelong bass player, took it from there, teaching him banjo, bass, and guitar. Forever restless, Red ventured through dozens of genres before returning to his Country roots. A firm believer that an artist’s greatest work is their life, Red always sought adventure beyond music in his wildly vacillating careers. Over only the past 5, he spent time working in National Parks and schools, bars and the backcountry, and most recently spending several years between the emergency department and ambulances across the country. Now settled into his high desert home Flagstaff, Arizona, Red has hit the road playing country music full tilt. In this first barnstorming year, he and his band will have played 31 states over 10 separate tours, logging over 25,000 miles and playing well over 250 shows a year with no end in sight. A first responder, passionate outdoorsman, recovering alcoholic, and heartbroken songwriter, whatever authenticity the country audience craves has been earned through his life, not place of birth. A self-proclaimed “Western fraud,” Red makes no effort to fit the country mold and rather draws from the reality of his life. Stranger-than-fiction characters and experiences from a life on the road mingle with honest, vulnerable expressions of a tumultuous life. events.summary: The year is 2056. We always knew they were out there…we just didn’t know they would attack so soon. Our city has fallen. Alien invaders and their cyborg forces have reduced the streets to rubble, and the few remaining survivors are doing whatever they can to escape. As if that weren’t enough, the destruction has brought another threat out of the shadows: zombies. This year’s interactive, no-contact haunted theatre drops you into the middle of the invasion. Choose how you face the apocalypse: Join the Resistance Rent an optional laser-tag weapon \(\+$2\) and fight back. The equipment uses a safe, invisible infrared beam to activate designated targets and trigger special effects as you move through the theatre. Become a Refugee Prefer not to use laser tag? Make your way through the ruined city as a refugee, trying to escape with your life while danger waits around every corner. Apocalypse in the Grove may include fog, laser lighting, loud noises, strobe effects, simulated fire, cold sparks, sudden scares, and intense theatrical environments. events.summary: Step into a sinful, spooky night of 1920s hot jazz and burlesque with the Ne Plus Ultra Jass Orchestra at historic Old Liberty Theater. Get ready for a sinful, spooky night of hot jazz, burlesque, and vintage glamour! The Ne Plus Ultra Jass Orchestra brings its 12-piece ensemble to the historic Old Liberty Theater in downtown Ridgefield for one night only with Hot Rhythms: A Sinful Cabaret Burlesque Revue. Known for presenting the hottest and most authentic classic jazz of the 1920s and 1930s, the Ne Plus Ultra Jass Orchestra will take you back to the era of Prohibition with a wicked collection of ghoulish, sultry, and downright irresistible tunes. Joining the orchestra for this special Halloween-weekend performance are acclaimed Pacific Northwest burlesque performers Natasha Riot, Cruz Daniels, and Wolfgang X. Together, the performers and musicians bring the storytelling, theatricality, and playful sensuality of classic burlesque to life, with the dancers performing alongside the live orchestra. Expect vintage jazz. Sinful rhythms. Spooky surprises. And a night of cabaret decadence you won't soon forget. This is a one-night-only event, so come dressed for the occasion, grab a drink, and prepare to be transported to a darker, sexier side of the Jazz Age. General Admission : $30 VIP Table: $150 A very limited number of premium VIP tables are available. Each VIP table includes admission for up to four guests plus one bottle of champagne. VIP tables are extremely limited and are expected to sell quickly. This event is strictly 21 and over. A Note About the Performance Burlesque is a theatrical art form rooted in comedy, dance, music, costume, and storytelling. The style of burlesque presented in this performance draws particularly from the classic burlesque tradition that developed in the early 20th century. Performances may include the tasteful removal of clothing as part of the storytelling and theatrical presentation. Performers do not become fully nude. This is a theatrical burlesque performance, not strip club or gentlemen's club style dancing. Some performers may interact with members of the audience as part of their acts. Consent is always key, and performers will not interact with audience members who appear uncomfortable. Tipping performers is an important part of burlesque culture. If you'd like to show your appreciation, please bring plenty of $1 bills. Cash will be available for withdrawal at the event, and QR codes will also be available for digital tips to individual performers. The content is adult in nature, but the overall performance would be comparable to approximately a PG-13 rating in film. Parking Street parking is available throughout downtown Ridgefield, but spaces can be limited, particularly for popular events. We recommend arriving early to allow time to find parking and get settled before the performance. Event Schedule 6:45 PM - Doors Open 7:30 PM - Performance Begins This event is made possible through the generosity of our media sponsor, the Clark County Historical Museum TICKETS ARE NON-REFUNDABLE/NON-TRASFERABLE
events.title: Hot Rhythms: A Sinful Cabaret Burlesque Revue

events.summary: Rock, Revolution. *LIZZIE* Brings America's Favorite Murder Mystery to Portland Marin Summer Theater and Bridgetown Conservatory of Musical Theatre present *LIZZIE* Music by Steven Cheslik-deMeyer, Alan Stevens Hewitt & Tim Maner Book and Lyrics by Tim Maner & Steven Cheslik-deMeyer What really happened inside the Borden house? Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. More information and tickets can be found at https:\\\\lizziepdx.com.

Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: 7pm doors 8pm show All ages welcome Great Lake Swimmers Featuring a blend of acoustic instruments, rural soundscapes, and wistful vocals, Great Lake Swimmers are a critically acclaimed indie-folk group led by Tony Dekker. Based in Southern Ontario, the group emerged in the early 2000s with a succession of heavily atmospheric albums recorded in old silos and rural country churches. The music developed in that pastoral warmth, performed and recorded in acoustically resonant and historical locales with a revolving cast of personnel. They are renowned for homespun folk and lush, intimate Americana in their live shows. Their newest album, Caught Light, released in October 2025, is their most immediate and instinctive album to date. Recorded in just five days in Ontario's Ganaraska Forest with producer Darcy Yates \(Bahamas\) and engineer Jimmy Bowskill \(Blue Rodeo\), it draws warmth from early '70s folk-pop while embracing a new spontaneity and directness in Dekker's songwriting. Great Lake Swimmers have been shortlisted for the prestigious Polaris Music Prize and nominated twice for Canada's Juno Awards, with the CBC calling them "a national treasure." "A stunning variety of tones and textures... nothing less than both cerebral and sublime" - American Songwriter, 4/5 "It floats from country to folk to indie rock and back again... a sharp-toothed but achingly beautiful portrait of the natural world and the human condition." - New Noise Magazine "Dekker's preoccupation with the Canadian state of mind flourishes in his lyrics. Few songwriters are able to convey the country's harsh beauty as well. ...Canadian folk tradition personified in the 21st century" - Exclaim! Website: https://greatlakeswimmers.com
events.title: Great Lake Swimmers - Caught Light Tour

events.summary: Since her debut, Soraya has solidified herself as a key tastemaker and driving force in California’s rising indie dance scene. Known for her dynamic and high-energy performances, the Filipino-American producer and DJ crafts genre-defying sets that pulse between house, techno, and indie dance. Her ability to fuse underground club aesthetics with euphoric, late-night energy has earned her a reputation as a must-see selector– captivating crowds across the United States. Her debut release ‘Brain Delay’ was released in early 2025 on Adam Ten & Mita Gami’s Maccabi House imprint alongside Broken Hill. The track garnered support from artists across the globe including Adam Ten, Mita Gami, Sam Shure, Audio Junkies, Enamour, Rafael, and more- alongside reaching Top 10 on Beatport’s Indie Dance Charts in the first day and has remained there since its release. In the past few years, Soraya has been a fixture at both major venues and underground parties, earning residencies and bookings at standout events such as Definition LA, Day Trip, Area15 Las Vegas, Midnight Lovers LA, Monarch SF, Music is 4 Lovers, Academy LA, and FNGRS CRSSD. She has shared stages with some of iconic names in the industry– providing direct support for artists like Mita Gami, Chaim, Deer Jade, Super Flu, andhim, Eli & Fur, Session Victim, and more. With a meticulous approach to sound design and a deep-rooted love for the underground, Soraya’s new chapter promises to further cement her as a force in the scene—one who doesn’t just play the music but shapes its future.

events.summary: Always on the go as one of the Pacific Northwest’s most trusted guitarists, Chance Hayden has performed avidly since the mid-00s as a chameleon-like musician who fluidly adapts through jazz, blues, funk and soul. Hayden's albums Get Somethin’ \(2018\) and Grab & Go \(2020\) were followed by the stand-alone single Shag Bag \(2022\) featuring iconic keyboardist Ronnie Foster of 70s-era George Benson fame. events.summary: PDX CONTEMPORARY ART is pleased to present Soñé Que Revelabas, a solo exhibition of new work by photographer Georgina Reskala. The works in the exhibition center on a dream the artist had last year in which she approached her late sister, who whispered to her “Soñé que revelabas” or “I dreamed that you revealed.” Revelar in Spanish means to manifest or make public something that was secret or unknown, and is also the chemical process in photography by which a latent image becomes visible. She awoke trying to make sense of this message and wrote the sentence on a piece of paper on her studio wall. As the days and months went by, Reskala realized that she was still trying to make sense of the loss of her sister. Loss of language, interactions, moments, and memories that become fainter as a result of distance and time. This body of work became a personal account of the process of translation, not just in language, but of sounds, inflections, stories, memories, and dreams. Working with silver gelatin prints and photographs printed on textile, Reskala explores this estrangement that comes with the inability to fully translate from one language to another. Using a variety of printing techniques, she repeatedly alters her images, adding and redacting information through material processes of physically manipulating the paper, unthreading the warp and weft of the linen, and by printing, rephotographing, and reprinting the same image multiple times.
events.title: Georgina Reskala ·

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape
events.title: Lookout Landscape Exhibition

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Please note that dogs are welcome on our deck and lawn areas—\[only Joey can come in the Sidereus Tasting House\]. For adults, join in the spirit of Halloween in costume with your friends. We’ll have treats for you too, while supplies last. Joey’s Story: A 4-pound Puff, the Smartest Dog, Best Friends Sidereus winery owners Skip and Ruth Tarr picked up Joey on Dec. 26, 2019 from a breeder in Scappoose, when he weighed only 4 pound. Since then, we think that Joey is the BEST and smartest dog in the whole world. Why? Ruth says that Joey is the smartest dog because after he learned more than 60 words, she quit counting. She elaborates that when she and Skip went through training with Joey, the trainer said that he was really training her and Skip, which explains how Joey started out knowing only his name and ‘sit,’ but his knowledge and vocabulary increased significantly after Ruth and Skip’s training was complete. Melissa, Sidereus wine tasting associate, also perfected Joey’s dance moves by teaching him how to ‘twirl.’ Joeys favorite things are steak, cauliflower, and playing with the ball and the water hose. His most favorite person is our winemaker Jason, who has Joey as a helper in winery production. Joey became an instant celebrity, made famous earlier this year when he was on-camera with Andy Carson of Good Day Oregon in a special feature that Andy led at Sidereus Winery last July. Joey is a small dog in stature. With all the coyotes in our vineyard are, he isn’t able to be outside by himself, as he thinks he’s a giant—but it’s really his heart that is big. He hasn’t found a human yet whom hasn’t become a friend.

It's 'vege-mania' in Wallace and Gromit's neighborhood, and our two enterprising chums are cashing in with their humane pest-control outfit, "Anti-Pesto." With only days to go before the annual Giant Vegetable Competition, business is booming, but Wallace & Gromit are finding out that running a "humane" pest control outfit has its drawbacks as their West Wallaby Street home fills to the brim with captive rabbits. Suddenly, a huge, mysterious, veg-ravaging "beast" begins attacking the town's sacred vegetable plots at night, and the competition hostess, Lady Tottington, commissions Anti-Pesto to catch it and save the day. Lying in wait, however, is Lady Tottington's snobby suitor, Victor Quartermaine, who'd rather shoot the beast and secure the position of local hero-not to mention Lady Tottingon's hand in marriage. With the fate of the competition in the balance, Lady Tottington is eventually forced to allow Victor to hunt down the vegetable chomping marauder. Little does she know that Victor's real intent could have dire consequences for her ...and our two heroes.

events.summary: The Altares y Muertos Tour is free and open to all, and it has become one of the most popular and beloved activities of the Milagro Central Eastside Muertos Celebration. Beginning at 11:30 AM, participants assemble in El Zócalo, the community gathering space at El Centro Milagro, and each guest is gifted a garland of silk marigolds to decorate themselves and their bicycles. Sometimes called zempachule or Flor de Muerto \(Flower of the Dead\), the marigold is an integral symbol of Día de Muertos. With their bright orange- and yellow-colored petals and strong fragrance, marigolds are believed to have the power to guide the souls of the dead back into the world of the living. At 12:00 PM, the first group of participants departs on a route around Portland’s Central Eastside, stopping intermittently at these partner businesses that are hosting altars as part of the Altares y Muertos Public Art Exhibition: Bar Botellón – 606 NE Davis St. Portland, OR 97214 Cargo – 81 SE Yamhill St. Portland, OR 97214 Cumbia Corazón – 222 SE 8th Ave, Portland, OR 97214 El Zócalo @ El Centro Milagro – 537 SE Stark St, Portland, OR 97214 New Deal Distillery – 900 SE Salmon St, Portland, OR 97214 Nossa Familia Coffee – 1633 SE 3rd Ave, Portland, OR 97214 Point West Credit Union – 1107 NE 9th Ave, Portland, OR 97232 River City Bicycles – 534 SE Belmont St., Portland, OR 97214 Along the way, they are guided by volunteers from The Street Trust, helping ensure everyone’s safety. This year, altars will be on public display beginning Saturday, October 24 and may be viewed during each business’ normal operating hours through Friday, November 6. \(A link to the map of all tour locations will be available for download on this page beginning Friday, October 23.\) The Altares y Muertos Tour will include a brief stop at the second annual Blumenauer Bridge Witching Hour, which takes place that day, but no altar is on display at that event.
events.title: Altares y Muertos Tour

events.summary: This exhibition highlights a distinct artistic collaboration between printmakers Cassie Ferguson and Charlie Cohan, marking the creative intersection of their independent yet interrelated studios, Lost Bearings Press (LBP) and BurnPrint Studio (BPS). Centered on a shared dedication to traditional printmaking, the showcase features a diverse range of techniques, including stone lithography, screen printing, polyester plate lithography, and relief printmaking. The conceptual foundation of this exhibition hinges on a collaborative print created by Cohan and Ferguson in 2017, which juxtaposed the iconic Burnside Skatepark with an urban overpass. This visual conversation continues in Ferguson’s ongoing series of stone lithographs capturing DIY skateparks. Her work seeks to honor and archive the subcultural spaces that have shaped her lived experience. Because these grassroots spaces often thrive under overpasses and within neglected industrial zones, her prints seamlessly connect with Cohan’s imagery of Portland’s monumental bridges. Together, the artists offer a multifaceted view of the city, championing the gritty beauty of structural environments. Their works invite viewers to reflect on their own relationship to the municipal landscape and to find new ways of seeing everyday urban scenes. Additionally, the exhibition introduces recent work by Nakemiah “Kiki” Williams, produced in collaboration with Ferguson and Cohan at LBP and BPS. This project marks the debut publication for LBP and brings their history full circle, as both Williams and Ferguson are alumnae of Cohan’s printmaking program at the University of Hawai’i at Mānoa. This collaboration marks the beginning of collaborative print work at LBP, which is now open for publishing and contracted prints of primarily stone lithographs.
events.title: Under the Overpass

events.summary: Fat Over Lean is a free art exhibition celebrating fat bodies, fat artists, and the many ways fatness intersects with queerness, disability, identity, and belonging. Curated by Portland artist Michelle Jackson, the exhibition brings together artwork by over 30 fat artists from across the Pacific Northwest, including painting, photography, fiber, ceramics, mixed media, and more. Created in response to the lack of positive and nuanced representation of fat bodies in the arts, Fat Over Lean is about making space for people whose bodies and experiences are too often left out of galleries. The exhibition will also feature free community events and creative programming throughout October. See works by Alexis Barnes, Ana Mai Luckett, Aurora Owen, Cherie Savoie Tintary, Eko Salamanca, Fi Bu, Garrett Stache, Heather Lobitz, Heather Weitman, Jessie Wu, Jo MahnkeVanHuss, Johnny Sheckler, JUUPI, KT Kusmaul / Body Home Fat Dance, Laura Grae Miller, Lyzz Stewart, M. V. Moran, Madison Flickinger, McKinley Johnson, Michelle Jackson, Morgan Wilhelm, Nat & Jess Breece, Richelle Fullerton, Roselynn La Jeunesse, Ruby Webb, Shaun Crabb, Shayla Smith, Shelby Fercik, Miss Joomina, Sossity Chiricuzio, Stevie Rosman-Hyde, Tarina Bagua, and Uwin Hakan. Join us for these upcoming events: Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3rd, 3- 8 p.m. Why Don't I Draw Myself Fat? Saturday, October 24th from 6 - 7:30 pm. A miniature Art Show and Telltale night of storytelling and taking up space in community hosted by Telltale Presents Closing Reception/Halloween Party: Saturday, October 31st, 7 - 9 pm. About Fat Over Lean Fat Over Lean is a project that aims to lower barriers to the arts for fat, queer, and disabled people by creating opportunities to share their work within the greater Portland, Oregon, and southern Washington communities. Artists were not charged a fee to apply for this show, and they will not pay a commission on artwork sold during the exhibition, aside from standard transaction fees. We believe artists should be able to share their work without having to navigate unnecessary financial barriers. By supporting fat artists, creators, and educators, Fat Over Lean hopes to create more opportunities for growth, visibility, advancement, and connection. This project is about making room: for fat bodies, for queer and disabled voices, for artists who are often asked to take up less space, and for the communities that grow when we get to show up as ourselves. This project was made possible by RACC, Portland Arts & Culture, Fans Only Studio, and Portland Clean Air Committee. Visit Fat Over Lean or Michelle's Instagram for events and gallery hours.
events.title: Fat Over Lean Art Show & Free Events

events.summary: By the pricking of my thumbs…Something wicked this way comes, one night only at the golden hour! Join Speculative Drama for the sixth annual one-hour adaptation of our internationally acclaimed 2020 production of Macbeth! This live, immersive, outdoor performance explores Shakespeare’s spookiest play from the perspective of Macbeth reliving the events leading up to his bloody and merciless reign, descent into madness, and death. Featuring a series of vignettes following the connective thread - “what makes a man a monster,” this fever dream production is a 55 minute runaway train of hilarious and haunting witches, bloody battles, and macabre madness - the perfect way to spend your Halloween weekend! Our audience is invited to meet at the oversized sidewalk chess set at the southeast corner of Director Park, and follow the Three Weird Sisters to a nearby outdoor arena. Trick or Treat bags are available before the show, because even adults deserve a little treat on Halloween. Walk-up audiences are welcome throughout the show, and this production is entirely FREE - though donations and tips to our hard working cast and crew are encouraged. Speculative Drama is a program under Misfit Academy, a performance oriented 501(c)3 and all donations and tips are 100% tax-deductible. Please note: All actors are fully vaccinated and tested day-of, audience masks are heavily encouraged for the safety of the actors. Anyone wearing a mask will be treated to a special gift, thank you for helping us keep our community safe and healthy! events.summary: The year is 2056. We always knew they were out there…we just didn’t know they would attack so soon. Our city has fallen. Alien invaders and their cyborg forces have reduced the streets to rubble, and the few remaining survivors are doing whatever they can to escape. As if that weren’t enough, the destruction has brought another threat out of the shadows: zombies. This year’s interactive, no-contact haunted theatre drops you into the middle of the invasion. Choose how you face the apocalypse: Join the Resistance Rent an optional laser-tag weapon \(\+$2\) and fight back. The equipment uses a safe, invisible infrared beam to activate designated targets and trigger special effects as you move through the theatre. Become a Refugee Prefer not to use laser tag? Make your way through the ruined city as a refugee, trying to escape with your life while danger waits around every corner. Apocalypse in the Grove may include fog, laser lighting, loud noises, strobe effects, simulated fire, cold sparks, sudden scares, and intense theatrical environments. Will you join the resistance—or simply try to survive? When you purchase a ticket, you purchase a reservation for a 30 minute window. You must arrive in this timeframe or your entry could be delayed or denied. There are 6 people in each tour of the haunted theatre. This experience is wheelchair accessible. And in her absence, Stella has begun a new life with her fiance, Bryan - an Earth Advocate who's devoted his life to saving what parts of Earth we still can. Over a single weekend, the trio work to find connection and healing after an undefined rupture that constantly threatens to rear its head. events.summary: Marsha Blovotnik is angry. So angry! The whole world is *fakakte*, but for this Leftie Jewish Lesbian, it’s her sister Janice who really burns her *tuchus*. Janice invites herself over for *Shabbos* dinner and then shows up three minutes early. Who does that?!? Just before her sister arrives, a mysterious ancestor gives Marsha a pot of magical chicken soup with the power to cure the world of its woes — if only Marsha can cool down enough to share a bowl of soup with her sister. A buoyant, crackling comedy about how to live in a dumpster fire.

events.summary: Rock, Revolution. *LIZZIE* Brings America's Favorite Murder Mystery to Portland Marin Summer Theater and Bridgetown Conservatory of Musical Theatre present *LIZZIE* Music by Steven Cheslik-deMeyer, Alan Stevens Hewitt & Tim Maner Book and Lyrics by Tim Maner & Steven Cheslik-deMeyer What really happened inside the Borden house? Based on the historical events surrounding the 1892 murders of Andrew and Abby Borden, LIZZIE explores the days leading up to the shocking crime through the eyes of four women (Voni Kengla as Lizzie Borden, Jessica Tidd as Emma Borden, Tia Lempert as Alice Russell, and Ashley Moore as Bridget Sullivan), determined to tell their own story. With a thunderous rock score inspired by artists such as Heart, The Runaways, and Bikini Kill, the musical is a bold examination of abuse, repression, freedom, and rage. The show has earned international acclaim, with productions in more than 100 theaters across 11 countries and multiple Best Musical awards. More information and tickets can be found at https:\\\\lizziepdx.com.

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

events.summary: Our audiences have been asking us to bring back the Halloween show for years…. Be careful what you wish for. Stephen Mallatratt’s The Woman in Black has been terrifying audiences since its London debut in 1987 and is one of the most successful and terrifying shows in West End history. Based on Susan Hill’s beloved novel, it’s one of the most celebrated ghost stories ever staged: atmospheric, relentless, and the kind of theatrical experience that makes you question every shadow on your way to the car. Set in a remote English village, it follows a young lawyer unraveling the secrets of a recently deceased client and the vengeful presence that doesn’t want him to. Just two actors portray all the characters, leaning into what B&B’s performers do best. Chilling, clever, and unforgettable. Halloween is back at Bag&Baggage…and we brought something with us. Show Dates: October 15 – November 1, 2026 Thu – Sat at 7:30pm, Sun at 2pm Special Dates: Thursday, October 15 is a preview performance, with discounted tickets. Friday, October 16, is Opening Night! Sat, Oct. 24th – ASL Interpreted Performance Sun, Oct. 25th – Audio Described Performance

events.summary: "Marigolds y Memorias" is an original devised production inspired by the traveling carpa tradition, in which humor, music, and storytelling come together in a vibrant theatrical journey. Guided by an elder, a younger generation learns to build an altar, the heart of Día de Muertos, discovering the meaning behind each of its elements, from candles and marigolds to photographs, ofrendas, and cherished recuerdos. Through song, dance, and short theatrical vignettes, the altar gradually takes shape as an act of remembrance and cultural inheritance, inviting audiences to consider how traditions are taught, how memory is kept alive, and what is carried forward when we share rituals across generations. Age Recommendation: All Ages Estimated Running Time: 1 hour 30 minutes, including one intermission
events.title: Marigolds y Memorias

events.summary: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. is a collection of four short, surreal plays by acclaimed English playwright, Caryl Churchill. Premiering at London's Royal Court Theatre in 2019, these darkly imaginative works weave together myth, fairy tale, and contemporary horror. Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. A girl made of glass. Gods and murders. A serial killer's friends. And a secret in a bottle.​ Four short plays by Caryl Churchill Directed by Samantha Van Der Merwe​October 10th - November 7th 2026
events.title: Glass. Kill. Bluebeard. Imp. by Caryl Churchill

events.summary: 7pm doors, 8pm show All ages welcome Patrick Wolf Patrick Wolf released his first E.P. at the age of 19, a groundbreaking debut of classical, folk, and electronic music that set the pace for a stellar decade, releasing seven self-produced and solely written albums and performing multiple laps around the globe on tour, amassing an ever-growing and dedicated, spellbound audience. A viola, piano, dulcimer, harp, lyre, and tenor guitar player, Patrick's decade of critically acclaimed work, touring, joining Patti Smith's band, collaborations with Florence Welch, Marianne Faithful, Angelo Badalamenti, and rapid, stellar ascent led to a sudden retreat from the industry where a decade of personal trial ended with a renaissance and reconnection with his work and vocation, documented in a feature film biopic documentary slated for release at the end of this year, executive produced by Tilda Swinton. Last year, he released his seventh album "Crying the Neck", an end-of-summer folkloric odyssey set in the landscape at the end of the East of England where Wolf lives and works. The album's success brought him back to his North American audiences; for his first tour in over 13 years, he embarked on a ten-week tour driving himself from east to west coast, where he discovered not only his fanbase had been waiting all that time, but a brand new one had grown in his absence in the States. The success of last year's tour brings Patrick back to North America this year with "The Tour of the Beast", this time an extensive East to West coast and back again routing with a coinciding 7" single and release campaign, launching two new songs to the States and ringing in the next era of Patrick Wolf. The first, a bombastic harpsichord banger and outsider anthem "The Beast", partly inspired by conversations had in the meet-and-greets of last year's tour and a hymn of solace, initially written as a response to Camus's "The Myth of Sisyphus", a lyre and vocal lullaby called "The Laughing Dove". The Guardian - "The Goth Folk Pioneer, A true one off" New York Times - "One of Britains most appealing singer songwriters" Lady Gaga - "Fantastic, Amazing, I listen to him, I meditate" Rolling Stone - "There's nothing not awesome about him" NME - "Britains foremost pop pioneer" Tilda Swinton - "My feeling is that we certainly come from the same planet: kith and kin. His music sounds like the great unexpressed soundtrack of a great film I want to see - and try to catch every night before I go to sleep.."
events.title: Patrick Wolf

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

events.summary: The Moreland Theater is proud to present WALLACE AND GROMIT: THE CURSE OF THE WERE-RABBIT (2005) as part of the Halloween themed Spooky Family Matinees screening series! The screening on Halloween 10/31 will feature a kids/family costume contest pre-show with prizes for our top three winners! So, come early if you'd like to participate. It's 'vege-mania' in Wallace and Gromit's neighborhood, and our two enterprising chums are cashing in with their humane pest-control outfit, "Anti-Pesto." With only days to go before the annual Giant Vegetable Competition, business is booming, but Wallace & Gromit are finding out that running a "humane" pest control outfit has its drawbacks as their West Wallaby Street home fills to the brim with captive rabbits. Suddenly, a huge, mysterious, veg-ravaging "beast" begins attacking the town's sacred vegetable plots at night, and the competition hostess, Lady Tottington, commissions Anti-Pesto to catch it and save the day. Lying in wait, however, is Lady Tottington's snobby suitor, Victor Quartermaine, who'd rather shoot the beast and secure the position of local hero-not to mention Lady Tottingon's hand in marriage. With the fate of the competition in the balance, Lady Tottington is eventually forced to allow Victor to hunt down the vegetable chomping marauder. Little does she know that Victor's real intent could have dire consequences for her ...and our two heroes.

events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: We Built You a Garden is the third installment of Metro’s Community Voices project, a multimedia storytelling initiative that invites residents of Metro Affordable Housing Bond-funded communities to explore the meaning of home through photography, writing and collective reflection. Hosted through a summer workshop series at the Strong Empowerment Village in partnership with artists Gwen Hoeffgen and Domenic Toliver, the project centers the experiences of residents with ties to North and Northeast Portland. Through weekly workshops and the use of film photography and creative writing, participants documented places, people and memories that shape their understanding of home, legacy and belonging. Their work considers displacement, resilience and community history, creating a powerful collection of stories that honor the past while imagining what can continue to grow. Ultimately, We Built You a Garden asks what’s been inherited, what’s been built, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. It speaks to the ongoing impact of displacement in Portland for the Black community, but it also affirms what it took — and continues to take — to nourish, tend and build home. Exhibition and events: Free admission Oct. 9, 5:30pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Exhibition Opening at The BLACK Gallery Join us for the opening of We Built You a Garden, with remarks and refreshments as well as free copies of the project’s publication. Open to public with remarks from Metro, artists, and Don’t Shoot PDX . Oct. 23, 6pm to 8pm: We Built You a Garden | Community Conversation at The BLACK Gallery A conversation about the past, present, and future of Portland through the experiences of the people who live, work, organize, and build here. Artists, activists, community members, youth and Metro come together to consider what we have inherited, what we have built, what is changing, and what we want to leave growing for the next generation. The BLACK Gallery will be open to the public on the following Sundays from 1pm to 4pm during the exhibition’s display: Oct. 11, Oct. 18, Oct. 25 and Nov. 1.
events.title: We Built You a Garden

events.summary: Set in the near future, when we have depleted Earth's resources and NASA has begun "colonizing" the Moon, Stella and Cassie meet for the first time in years. But this is no ordinary reunion - these fraternal twins have been separated by more than just years and miles. And in her absence, Stella has begun a new life with her fiance, Bryan - an Earth Advocate who's devoted his life to saving what parts of Earth we still can. Over a single weekend, the trio work to find connection and healing after an undefined rupture that constantly threatens to rear its head. events.summary: Sundays 4:30PM - 5:30PM, Oct 4 - Dec 20 | $10/weekly drop in Need a reset for your busy week ahead? Join us Sunday late afternoons for a welcoming, beginner-friendly yoga class focused on foundational poses, mindful movement, breath awareness, and building confidence on the mat. Whether you’re brand new to yoga or looking to reconnect with the fundamentals, this class is designed to help you build a strong foundation through accessible movement, breath work, and foundational poses. We’ll focus on alignment, balance, flexibility, and body awareness in a welcoming, supportive environment. Beginners are encouraged to join, and those with a regular practice will also benefit from slowing down, refining technique, and deepening their understanding of familiar poses. Options and modifications will be offered throughout class so everyone can move at their own pace. Wear comfortable athletic clothes, bring a yoga mat if possible \(a limited number will be available to borrow\), and please arrive 5–10 minutes before class begins so we can start on time. Classes are led by Wyle O'Neill, from Love Our Practice, whose yoga journey began in high school and later led him to study in Mysore and Goa, India, where he deepened his understanding of yoga’s roots and philosophy. Wyle completed his 200-hour RYT training at Yoga Salt with Tamal Dodge and completed his 500-hour teacher training at Sthira Yoga School in Goa, India. His teaching blends accessible movement, meditation, breathwork through an individual-centered practice to help students feel grounded, present, as well as connected to themselves and community.

events.summary: At a time when many theatres are closing their doors or reducing programming, 100 Lives Repertory in Portland’s Buckman neighborhood is celebrating the inaugural season in its brand-new space. And the first play is a doozy: a sleek, sly, sci-fi mystery titled Anthropology, penned by Lauren Gunderson, one of America’s most produced playwrights. Anthropology is about a grieving computer coder, Merril, who builds an AI replica of her missing and presumed dead sister. Adding to the loss, Merril’s relationship with her girlfriend has come to an end, which draws her deeper and deeper into her ‘project’ of bringing back a version of her sister, to help heal her grief and lessen her loneliness. This is the Oregon premiere of Anthropology which had its world debut in London at Hampstead Theatre in 2023. The play runs Thursday through Sunday from October 23 through November 15. It features an all-female, four-actor cast and is directed by 100 Lives Rep’s Executive Director Cat Plein. Due to nudity and sexual situations, it is recommended only for adult audiences.

Moving between collective voices and intimate encounters, Churchill explores violence, power, desire, and the stories we tell to make sense of a fractured world. By turns funny, haunting, and unsettling, the plays invite audiences into a landscape where the familiar becomes strange and ancient myths reveal modern anxieties without explanation or comfort. events.summary: 6pm doors, 7pm show All ages welcome Taylor Bickett Taylor Bickett is a storyteller at heart. Hailing from Indiana, she's been writing music since before she can remember. Taylor's intimate lyrics and outstanding vocal range gracefully overlay organic indie pop production to create introspective singer/songwriter tunes. After her wistful, Gen Z anthem "QUARTER LIFE CRISIS" hit the internet in 2022, the track compelled a generation struggling with their newfound adulthood to share their own photos and stories on TikTok soundtracked by her song. The trending audio amassed nearly half a million fan-made videos, and celebrities including Drew Barrymore and Kevin Jonas showcased their own transformations since age sixteen atop Taylor's track, which features the lyrics, "I swear 16 was yesterday, but now I'm closer to 28." Taylor's subsequent 2023 EP grown up and lonely demonstrates her knack for writing honest and unfiltered songs that resonate with an entire generation. She kicked off 2024 with her single "I Like Mondays" which resonated with fans when she quickly wrote and posted the song on the 1st of January \(a Monday\). After spending the spring on the road, Taylor released her second EP, This Isn't Me Missing You, on September 19th. Taylor spent 2024 touring with artists like Ron Pope, Blü Eyes, Andi and Áine Deane, which took her all over the US and UK. Her new song "The Crime," based on a traumatic incident that sparked a passion for ending violence against women, will come out in honor of Women's History Month in March of 2025. She is currently writing new music for her debut full length album.
events.title: Taylor Bickett

THE EXPERIENCE Join us for a screening of Union County, starring Will Poulter and Noah Centineo alongside a cast of non-actors from central Ohio. Set in the shadow of the opioid epidemic, this hopeful drama follows two brothers navigating court-mandated recovery, and the community that helps them imagine a different future. Ohio-born filmmaker Adam Meeks drew inspiration from the real-life recovery community he met in his hometown, which was full of people healing and getting their lives back. Some of them were cast in the film, and the result is an intimate, compassionate portrait of people rebuilding their lives and finding solidarity and hope in the aftermath of a devastating drug crisis. "Will Poulter is staggering."-Marhsall Shaffer, THE PLAYLIST "It feels like someone opened a door to the real world."-Bilge Ebiri, VULTURE ON SCREEN: Union County 2026. Directed by Adam Meeks. Runtime: 1 hour 37 minutes. Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor \(Annette Deao\), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future. Poulter and Centineo blend seamlessly with a supporting cast composed predominantly of non-professional actors as they share their actual experiences, pain, and optimism as they, themselves, navigate the program. Ohio-born filmmaker Adam Meeks creates a film imbued with realism for an honest, compassionate portrait of a battle being fought across America and the solidarity that flowers on its front lines. events.summary: Skeletons Out of the Closet The annual Spooky Art Show returns to Lavaun's Community Gallery for its third year, this time as “Skeleton's Out of the Closet.” Curated from an open call for submissions, this show features art that is spooky, scary, strange, and out of the ordinary. Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

events.summary: We live in a world that seems to be obsessed with youth. The insights and wisdom of those of us who are aging is too often ignored, leaving seniors feeling passed over and left behind. The baby boomer generation is aging, the last of this generation will reach age 65 by 2030, it’s time to validate ourselves in a world that honors youth. This workshop is designed to take the stress \(and expensive effort\) out of the aging process. We can’t avoid wrinkles, but we still can celebrate and demonstrate to ourselves and others, self-acceptance and validate our expertise, experience, and importance. This workshop helps identify us as role models who engage in self-acceptance, pride, and higher self-esteem as we clearly define our elegant aging self. This workshop is facilitated by Mara Woloshin, who helps lead participants on a positive pathway of individual positive self-discovery. This free and educational workshop will be facilitated by licensed broker Mara Woloshin, who works in Medicare and in health care services, including education and advocacy. This Event is 21\+ ---------------------------------------- After many years celebrating the music of Big Star via the collective known as Big Star’s Third, Jody Stephens \(the last surviving member of the original Big Star lineup\) had an idea. “I truly loved touring the world and performing Big Star’s Third with a core group, a variety of special guests, and a chamber orchestra playing the beautiful orchestrations created by Carl Marsh and Chris Stamey. But when the idea of celebrating the 50th anniversary of \#1 Record came up, it was time to pare the production down to a five-piece rock band. So I called a few close and like-spirited musical friends.” Enter some of the legendary group’s biggest fans, who have long been associated with Big Star and related projects. The band now includes Mike Mills \(R.E.M.\), Jon Auer \(The Posies\), Pat Sansone \(Wilco\), Chris Stamey \(The dB's\) and Stephens. Dubbing themselves the Big Star Quintet, it’s a lineup that is both personal and close in spirit to \#1 Record and Radio City.
events.title: Big Star Quintet

events.summary: Help spread warmth and kindness this holiday season as Vancouver Mall joins Centennial Real Estate's nationwide Share the Warmth campaign in partnership with One Warm Coat! From October 1 through December 31, the community is invited to donate new or gently worn coats to help local individuals and families stay warm during the colder months. Every coat makes a difference! Guests can drop off donations at designated collection locations throughout Vancouver Mall, including the SEE Centennial Donation Dropbox near Macy's, the Vancouver Mall Management Office, and select seasonal collection sites. Donations will benefit local community members in need, helping ensure more neighbors have access to warm outerwear this winter. Throughout the campaign, Vancouver Mall will also host special donation opportunities and community events, including National Share the Warmth Day on October 20, featuring family-friendly activities, warm beverages, and special donor appreciation experiences. events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists

Alberta Street Gallery member Julia Alora, a lifetime lover of Halloween, has hand-picked this year’s collection of frights and delights from more than 10 local artists. What makes art spooky? Art that focuses on fears, phobias, or disquieting themes. Settings or characters or creatures that are dark, born from night, or upsetting to see. Images that capture the fun and nostalgia of playing in a scary space through a safe lens, reminiscent of horror movies and Halloweens past. Come in for a thrill and a chill, find a new piece to haunt your home, and enjoy beautiful works of art perfect for those who are strange and unusual. Alberta Street Gallery is a friendly and vibrant cooperative gallery of 30 local artists in the heart of the Alberta Arts District in Northeast Portland. In addition to our members’ art, we mount monthly shows that begin on the “Last Thursday” of every month. Our front windows feature new work by two of our member artists, and we curate group shows in Lavaun's Community Gallery, a special exhibition space inside the gallery named for and made possible by gallery member Lavaun Benavidez Heaster, a legally blind collage artist who died in 2020.

She released her debut album, Same Time Tomorrow, in August 2024, establishing herself as a distinctive voice in contemporary folk and indie music. Her sophomore album, Pumpkin \(March 20, 2026\), is largely self-produced and further defines her richly textured, sonically delicate sound. Rooted in indie folk, chamber pop, and indie rock, Pumpkin explores the limits of emotional self-protection. Beneath that guarded exterior, the songs return to an inner child still longing for safety, tenderness, and rest - a theme distilled, somewhat wryly, in the album's title and final track, "Pumpkin," a term of endearment that gestures toward softness rather than defense. Haunting, cinematic, and deeply reflective, Parker crafts immersive, emotionally resonant songs that balance vulnerability with sharp, intelligent lyricism.

events.summary: Lookout Landscape is an immersive art exhibition by Oregon-based artist and designer David Buckley Borden and a team of collaborators working across forestry, design, and engineering. Inspired by fire lookout towers, trail culture, and backcountry gear, the exhibition invites visitors onto a fabricated “Lookout Trail,” where a series of imaginative scenes—from a trailhead to a weather station, campground, and tool shed—reimagine the visual language of forestry and outdoor culture in the Pacific Northwest. Blending research, humor, and design, the exhibition explores the complex relationships between people and working forests, with wildfire as an underlying thread. As visitors move through the space, they are encouraged to reflect on how forests are shaped, valued, and cared for, and to consider their own connection to these landscapes. Plan your visit and explore the exhibition: worldforestry.org/lookout-landscape

events.summary: This former Southern Pacific Railroad station, fondly called the Old Train Station \(OTS\), is home to Friends of Historic Forest Grove. The Old Train Station now serves as a museum highlighting about 150 years of local history, from photographs and maps to clothing and furniture. It also houses an historic library and research center. Built in 1913, the station handled passenger and light freight service into 1929. After that only light freight came through. Burlingham and Sons purchased the building as office space for their seed company. Unfortunately, over the years this building has gone through some internal and external changes but some of the original station remains and can easy be found. Woodfold acquired the building from Burlingham and has graciously allowed Friends to use the building since 2008. Please stop by and see what we have to offer. Check website to confirm open hours
events.title: Friends of Historic Forest Grove Museum & Library Open

events.summary: Curated by Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School and Lisa Jarrett Drawing from the Museum’s collection, this exhibition is co-curated by Lisa Jarrett, an artist, educator, and curator, and the Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK Elementary— a group of 4th and 5th grade curators from KSMoCA. Working from a conversation with notable curators Dr. Lowery Stokes Sims and Dr. Leslie King Hammond, the exhibition engages PAM’s collection in new dialogues shaped by emerging curatorial voices and multigenerational knowledge. From theme and concept development, through work selection, and installation, this community curators project highlights the collaborative nature of curatorial practice and museum work. Harriet Tubman Center for Expanded Curatorial Practice at MLK School \(HTC\) is a KSMoCA project. Students participate directly in shaping exhibitions, positioning them as contributors to the museum, and engaging them as researchers, writers, planners, and curators. Through workshops and field trips, students collaborate with artists, visiting curators, and mentors from Portland State University’s College of the Arts. They research how exhibitions are developed, how artworks are interpreted, and how institutional decisions shape public understanding. Expanded curatorial practice includes visual art, writing, performance, research, publishing, and social practice. Co-founded by Lisa Jarrett and Harrell Fletcher, the project began in 2018 at Harriet Tubman Middle School and continues in its current iteration at Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary School.
events.title: Harriet Tubman Center Museum

events.summary: Inspired by Katherine Ace’s 9 Portraits as the foundational starting point for the exhibition, Nine Women Artists will feature the work of the artists shown in Ace’s portrait painting. All mature artists in their careers and with a significant presence in the Northwest, their work reveals a diverse expression of artistic styles from representation to abstraction. There are rich details in the painting. Most notably on the left hangs Henri Fantin-Latour’s A Studio at Les Batignolles, 1870 \(Musée d’Orsay\). In this painting is a formal gathering of male artists. In response to this painting, Katherine asked her subjects to dress in their studio/work clothes as counterpoint, all marked in their characteristic poses. Other Portland women artists are recognized here through their paintings—a small Sally Haley still life hangs in the background, as well as an Amanda Snyder painting behind Phyllis Yes. And to the far right, we have a glimpse of Lucinda Parker’s very large work. Postcards and newspapers scattered on the floor are the exhibition announcements and reviews highlighting the artists’ works. An epic portrait featuring nine women artists of the Northwest, Ace responded to the lack of self-portraits by women artists in history. From left, the artists are: Laura Ross-Paul, Katherine’s self-portrait seated with phone, Mary Josephson, Judy Cooke, Phyllis Yes, Sharon Bronzan, Shu-Ju Wang, Lucinda Parker, and Sherrie Wolf. All are women artists who have made long careers in Portland. As Ace notes about these women, “They have tenacity, have lived through sexist decades, told they couldn’t really be artists—only fit for sleeping with the professor, expected to subvert themselves to male artist machismo.”
events.title: Nine Women Artists
